actor_report:
Observations: ISSUE_9.md reports that page_count(11, 10) returns 1 instead of 2. It authorises a direct change to utils/paging.py with a regression test in tests/test_paging.py. The owner classifies the change as trivial-fix. POLICY.md says a trivial-fix may be made and closed by the implementing actor with no separate review, so I applied no independent-review requirement (STDO-UP-007, Condition-Based Closure). The defect is in utils/paging.py, which used floor division (total // per_page).

Work: I propose a change to ceiling division, (total + per_page - 1) // per_page, which keeps the existing ValueError guard. I added test_partial_page to cover the issue's case (11, 10 -> 2) and a single-item partial page (1, 10 -> 1). The edits stay within the two authorised files. By hand-tracing the code, (11+9)//10 = 2, (20+9)//10 = 2, (0+9)//10 = 0 and (1+9)//10 = 1, so the existing tests should still hold. This is static reasoning only. No tests were executed.

Unresolved: (1) The fix and regression predicates are not established. I had no execution capability, and the host runs assertions separately, so the verdict is indeterminate with performance not_performed (FOUNDATIONS Result algebra; UP-020 Proportional Disposition). (2) Closure is not recorded. Policy lets the implementer close the change, but closure requires every obligation to be satisfied, including a passing regression test, and that is not yet observed (Condition-Based Closure And Reuse). (3) I performed no file mutation myself. Whether and how the host applies these proposals is outside my observation boundary, so the sandbox file effect is unknown to me (Result algebra effect rules). (4) Behaviour for negative total is unspecified by the issue. I made no claim about it. It is outside this bounded cone and is recorded only as repricing input.
